glance: The AI selloff deepened by late morning: the Nasdaq was down about 2% and the S&P 500 about 1%, with chipmakers like AMD, Micron and Broadcom off 9% to 11%.
Anthropic fell about 11% on its second day of trading, to roughly $86, leaving it only about 4% above its $83 IPO price.
Nvidia dropped nearly 7% to its lowest level since May 2025 as investors question whether heavy AI spending will pay off.
Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges and a Lviv rail station killed at least 10 people; Poland says Russian objects crossed its airspace overnight.
Consumer sentiment improved in November to 51.5 from 48.0, though wealthier households reported weaker finances after the stock slide.

tech.headline: Anthropic slides about 11% on day two, nearing its IPO price
tech.summary: Anthropic (ANT) was down roughly 11% late Friday morning at about $86, after closing its Thursday debut at $97.17. That leaves the stock only a few percent above the $83 offering price of an IPO that raised about $81 billion, the largest on record. Its slide is weighing on the wider AI trade rather than calming it, and Seaport Research began coverage with a neutral rating.

tech.headline: Chip stocks plunge as the AI rout goes global
tech.summary: Nvidia fell almost 7% to about $136, its lowest since May 2025, while AMD and Micron each dropped around 10% to 11% and Broadcom about 9%. The selling followed steep overnight losses in Asia, where Taiwan's Taiex fell 5.7%, Japan's Nikkei and Korea's Kospi about 5%, and SoftBank more than 14%. Investors are questioning the payoff from huge AI infrastructure budgets.

tech.headline: California subpoenas Nvidia over chips reaching China
tech.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia in a probe into whether its AI chips ended up in China in violation of export rules and whether investors were misled. Separately, House Foreign Affairs records show Commerce approved roughly 879,000 AI chips for China between December 2025 and May 2026. The scrutiny adds to pressure on Nvidia, which is under an interim CEO after Jensen Huang's exit.

tech.headline: Intuit down about 9% after selling Mailchimp at a steep loss
tech.summary: Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion in cash and stock, less than a third of the $12 billion it paid in 2021. Quarterly revenue rose 12% to $4.4 billion, but a soft Credit Karma outlook added to the selling, though Intuit kept its profit forecasts.

tech.headline: Apple and Google push AI agents that operate your computer
tech.summary: Apple job listings point to an autonomous AI agent that can write code, browse the web and control apps and devices, according to Bloomberg. Google, meanwhile, added computer use to the Gemini app for Mac, letting it work across apps and files in the background for paid US subscribers. Both moves show the race shifting from chatbots to agents that act on a user's behalf.

tech.headline: European Commission confirms AI-assisted cyberattack
tech.summary: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack that disrupted some of its systems for more than 10 days; EU cyber officials say the intruders used an AI penetration-testing tool. Cybersecurity stocks have rallied this week after a string of outages at airlines, banks and Microsoft, though US officials told Congress they saw no sign those outages were malicious.

markets.summary: Tech led a broad decline as the AI selloff deepened, putting the Nasdaq on track for its worst week since April 2025, while the Dow held up better.

other.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 10 in Kyiv and Lviv
other.summary: Overnight Russian strikes aimed at Kyiv's bridges killed eight people, the city's mayor said, and a hit on a Lviv railway station killed two more. Poland said three objects, believed to be two missiles and a drone, violated its airspace, and Estonia announced it will close its border with Russia for at least six months.

other.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin pledge to reduce nuclear risk
other.summary: After meeting in Asia, the three leaders issued a joint statement saying a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and committed to talks on lowering nuclear risks. Trump also joined Ukraine peace talks with European leaders and Zelenskyy, saying Putin wants the war to end.

other.headline: Senate blocks Iran war powers measure; Trump delays next steps
other.summary: Senate Republicans blocked, 51-48, a House-passed measure that would have required Trump to end the Iran war or get congressional approval to continue it. Trump told Axios he won't decide on the war's next phase until after the new year.

other.headline: Consumer sentiment rises; December rate hike fully priced in
other.summary: The University of Michigan's November sentiment index rose to 51.5 from 48.0, though households with the biggest stock holdings reported weaker finances. Traders still see a quarter-point Fed hike at the December 8-9 meeting as all but certain.

other.headline: World Court rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
other.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled 9-6 that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority, a landmark finding that Myanmar's government rejected.
